newsitem.title: POLAND: Ten dead, 15 badly injured in Polish train crash.
newsitem.headline: Ten dead, 15 badly injured in Polish train crash.

text.p: Ten people died and 15 were seriously injured when several coaches decoupled from a passenger train, left the track and hit a stationary goods train near Szczecin in northwest Poland on Monday, police said.
"We have confirmed that there are 10 dead... 15 badly injured and another 15 less badly hurt," Szczecin police deputy spokesman Krzysztof Rusinowicz told Reuters.

He said he had no details yet of the identity or nationality of the victims of the accident at the small station of Reptowo near Stargard Szczecinski, south of Szczecin and not far from the German border.

Police earlier said the wagons came uncoupled from the end of the fast train, travelling from the coastal town of Swinoujscie to Krakow in the south, at about 12.25 p.m. (1025 GMT) and struck the goods train on a nearby line.

Rusinowicz said rescuers were still working at the scene and Transport Minister Boguslaw Liberadzki had set out from Warsaw for Szczecin where he would call a special commission to investigate the cause of the accident.
PAP news agency quoted a Szczecin fire brigade spokesman as saying that a child was among the dead.
